name: Bun
tagline: A JavaScript runtime, bundler, test runner, and package manager.
hook: Tests must fail against the installed runtime and pass against the local build.
summary: Bun makes its build wrapper the default route into development and testing, with an explicit exception for declaration-only edits. Its instructions distinguish real regressions from behavior that never worked, explain how debug and sanitizer builds change test costs, and route specialized review decisions to separate guides. AGENTS.md is a symlink to this CLAUDE.md source.

techniques.title: Prove that the test detects the change
techniques.body: The guide requires a failing run against the installed Bun and a passing run against the debug build. A green test against both is not accepted as evidence for the fix.
techniques.quote: Verify your test fails with `USE_SYSTEM_BUN=1 bun test <file>` and passes with `bun bd test <file>`. Your test is NOT VALID if it passes with `USE_SYSTEM_BUN=1`.

techniques.title: Explain the exception to the build rule
techniques.body: Type declaration tests package declaration files and invoke TypeScript without running the native binary. The guide therefore allows the installed test runner for this specific case.
techniques.quote: Edits to **TypeScript type declarations** (`packages/bun-types/**/*.d.ts`) do not touch any compiled code, so `bun bd` is unnecessary. The types test just packs the `.d.ts` files and runs `tsc` against fixtures — it never executes your build. Run it directly with the system Bun (an explicit exception to the "never use `bun test` directly" rule):

techniques.title: Define what counts as a regression
techniques.body: An issue-numbered regression file requires both a real issue and previously working behavior. Other bug coverage belongs beside the existing tests for the module.
techniques.quote: If the behavior was never correct, it's not a regression — the test belongs in the existing file for that module.

techniques.title: Budget for debug and sanitizer overhead
techniques.body: The test guidance gives approximate time budgets and explains why release-speed assumptions become expensive in CI. It also distinguishes timeout ceilings from targets.
techniques.quote: Keep tests fast: budget roughly 1s per test and 10s per file. Debug+ASAN builds run 10-100x slower than release, so a 1s local test can take a minute in CI.

techniques.title: Account for arena cleanup semantics
techniques.body: The memory-management note names the exception to normal RAII cleanup: arena reset does not run destructors. Heap allocations and references owned by those values need explicit release first.
techniques.quote: Arena edge case: values allocated in an arena (`Arena<T>`/`bumpalo`) do **not** run `Drop` on arena reset — types owning a heap allocation or refcount must be freed/deref'd explicitly first, mirroring the original Zig `deinit()` order.

techniques.title: Route review decisions by task
techniques.body: The root links the shared review rules and a situational guide covering compatibility, API design, performance, platforms, dependencies, documentation, and PR work.
techniques.quote: Several situational sections live in `.claude/docs/landing-prs.md` — read the relevant one before the work it covers:

steal: Require a regression test to distinguish the installed build from the changed build.
Document precise exceptions next to broad command prohibitions.
Define terms such as regression before using them to organize tests.
Set test budgets with CI instrumentation overhead in mind.
Call out lifetime-management exceptions that ordinary language idioms hide.
outline: Landing PRs: What Bun Reviewers Catch
